      <p>My research focuses on <strong>machine learning</strong> and <strong>signal processing</strong> for relational data, including graphs and higher-order structures. I study how mathematical structure can guide the design of scalable, stable, and interpretable learning models. I am also interested in applications in computer vision, circuit design, environmental monitoring, materials analysis, physical systems, and underwater acoustics.</p>
      <p>I received my PhD in Applied Mathematics from La Rochelle Université in 2022. Before my doctoral studies, I worked on graph signal processing at the University of Delaware and completed my MSc and BSc degrees at Universidad de Antioquia, Colombia.</p>

## Research interests

My work lies at the intersection of learning, signal processing, and structured data. The main themes are:

```{=html}
<ul class="research-interest-list">
  <li><strong>Machine learning on graphs and higher-order structures.</strong> Graph neural networks, continuous models, and geometric learning on graphs, hypergraphs, simplicial complexes, and cellular complexes.</li>
  <li><strong>Graph signal processing.</strong> Learning graph structure and developing methods for reconstruction, forecasting, imputation, summarization, stability, and generalization.</li>
  <li><strong>Scientific and engineering applications.</strong> Structured-learning methods for vision, wildlife monitoring, underwater acoustics, materials, physical simulation, image compression, and circuit design.</li>
</ul>
```
